recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-9812 unless a future editorial pass chooses to polish wording while preserving current authorization naming and aliases.
issue_request: FHIR-9812 was a Published Security change request with a Persuasive with Modification resolution to add an AuditEvent note explaining PurposeOfEvent at the event level and PurposeOfUse at the agent level, including omission when purpose is unknown and differences between reporting perspectives.
initial_application: Git commit 7755ff73d6, "Security WG updates to GF#9150, GF#9151, GF#9812, GF#9840, GF#9919, and GF#10046," added a PurposeOfEvent/PurposeOfUse section to source/auditevent/auditevent-notes.xml in the active AuditEvent resource source.
additional_context: Later Published issue FHIR-32515 changed AuditEvent purposeOfEvent and agent.purposeOfUse to authorization and agent.authorization, lowered the PurposeOfUse binding to example, and kept PurposeOfEvent/PurposeOfUse as aliases. Current source/fhir.ini maps the old names to the current names, and the current StructureDefinition and note reflect the later model. Direct community searches found no FHIR-9812-specific conflicting record; broader Zulip and Confluence evidence supports the later authorization/PurposeOfUse context.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current note explains whole-event and per-agent purpose-of-use guidance, omission when unknown, and differing reporter perspectives using current element names; reverting to the original DSTU2 names would make the current build less accurate.

related_jiras.note: Renamed AuditEvent purposeOfEvent/agent.purposeOfUse to authorization/agent.authorization, changed binding strength, and explains why FHIR-9812's old element names are now aliases rather than current primary names.
